steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Conjunct melody moves by step (adjacent notes); disjunct melody leaps between distant notes — each creates different character. | Key Fact: Triadic melodies outline chord shapes; scalic melodies run up/down scales; arpeggio melodies break chords into individual notes. | Key Fact: Passing notes connect chord notes melodically; ornamental notes (acciaccatura, appoggiatura) decorate the main melody. | Key Fact: Ostinato is a repeated melodic pattern that provides a foundation — used extensively in Baroque, minimalism and popular music.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe how melody are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use melody. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use melody in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.
